question: Why did the error rate go up on 07 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: Upstream search-cluster is experiencing degraded performance, causing service search to fail with HTTP 503 and timeouts.
why_chain: The upstream search-cluster is returning HTTP 503, indicating it is down or overloaded.
The search-cluster is failing to respond within the retries, causing service search to time out.
The search-cluster is experiencing degraded performance, leading to the error rate increase in service search.

contributing_factors.description: The error rate increase is concentrated in service search, suggesting a specific issue with this service.
why_chain: The error rate increase is not uniform across all service/region segments.
The error rate increase is specifically in service search, indicating a localized issue.
The localized issue in service search is likely related to the upstream search-cluster.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a sudden surge in user traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for service search did not change significantly, and the error rate increase is concentrated in service search.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a configuration change in service search.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a configuration change that would cause the error rate to increase.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a change in infrastructure, such as network or server capacity.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a change in infrastructure that would cause the error rate to increase.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to bad or unusual input data.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of bad or unusual input data that would cause the error rate to increase.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service search rose from 0.35% to 3.74% (+965%), with a change point at 2026-03-07T05:30:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service search: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.12).
At the same time, request volume for service search stayed about the same (2454 per 5 min before, 2862 per 5 min after, +17%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service search rose (141 ms before, 253 ms after, +80%).
Upstream search-cluster returning HTTP 503 for search (search; 2 min after the change; record R014)
search: ERROR upstream search-cluster timeout after 3 retries (search, us-east; 5 min after the change; record R015)
search: ERROR upstream search-cluster timeout after 3 retries (search, ap-south; 10 min after the change; record R016)
search: ERROR upstream search-cluster timeout after 3 retries (search, eu-west; 19 min after the change; record R017)

Monitor the upstream search-cluster and take preemptive actions if it shows signs of degradation.
